summary: Framing, value profile and library choices are specified closely enough to build, but the protocol's own message set is not: the biggest gap is the undefined handshake/entry messages and the wire form of envelope-level HostCallError.

questions.text: Is a Completed result committed on receipt of the complete frame or only after a clean guest exit, and what happens to trailing bytes or a nonzero exit after it?
questions.reason: Atomicity of result publication; the ADR only says a partially written frame never publishes a result and tests cover trailing garbage.

questions.text: How is an envelope-level HostCallError encoded on the wire when the plugin HostResponse result holds only the declared Either FetchError a?
questions.reason: Decides the guest decoder and how abort is told apart from resuming with Left; the ADR says undeclared errors abort and the result has no second error wrapper, but gives no wire slot for HostCallError.

questions.text: What do the handshake and initial-entry messages contain (including snapshot), and where and how are contract identities checked?
questions.reason: Fixes the first frames of the state machine and where the repair instruction is raised; the ADR says identities are checked before a typed entry input and the plugin begins with {arguments, snapshot}, but explicitly leaves these cases unexpanded.

questions.text: How are multi-field positional constructors and record-syntax constructors inside a sum type encoded?
questions.reason: Wire shape generated identically on both peers; the table covers only nullary and single-value cases, and newtype wrappers are tagged or objects.

questions.text: Which type formers beyond records, sums, lists, Text and Bool (maps, sets, tuples, unit, Char, ByteString fields) are supported, and how is each encoded?
questions.reason: Sets generator coverage and wire shapes; the ADR says only 'supported, compiler-inspected authored ADTs' and that unsupported mappings must be rejected.

questions.text: What exact grammar do canonical numeric (and date/instant) strings follow, and must decoders reject non-canonical spellings?
questions.reason: Both peers must agree on one spelling for encoded values; the ADR mandates canonical decimal strings never via Double but says exact decimal syntax is separate.

questions.text: Does structural decoding reject or ignore object keys the target constructor does not declare?
questions.reason: Changes every generated decoder and conformance expectations; the ADR covers duplicate keys, unknown tags and missing fields but not extra keys.

questions.text: Who allocates request IDs and what counts as a wrong ID: mismatch with the outstanding request only, or also reuse, gaps or a fixed start?
questions.reason: Changes host validation state and wrong-ID tests; the ADR says IDs are canonical integer strings and wrong IDs abort, with one outstanding request.

questions.text: How are HTTP headers represented in metadata (object vs ordered pairs), and are names case-normalised?
questions.reason: An object under first-key-wins would drop repeated headers like Set-Cookie; the ADR only says metadata contains method/URL/headers or status/headers.

questions.text: What happens when a raw HTTP response body is not valid UTF-8 given the typed HTTP boundary is UTF-8 text?
questions.reason: Failure classification (Left, lossy decode or protocol abort) and whether error pages reach the provider; the ADR says the boundary stays UTF-8 text and non-2xx bodies are retained.

questions.text: Is there any cap on total section or message size beyond the 64 KiB chunk limit?
questions.reason: Host assembles sections before decoding, so an unbounded guest can exhaust memory; the ADR says chunk size is not a limit on total message size but names no other limit.

questions.text: Is there a host-enforced deadline or idle timeout for a guest that never sends its next frame, and who configures it?
questions.reason: Otherwise only outer cancellation stops a hung guest; the ADR only says no orphan guest waits forever for a host response.

questions.text: When a nested child plugin invocation fails fatally, does the parent receive a handleable typed value or does the outer invocation abort?
questions.reason: Fixes result types of the nested-call capability; the ADR says recoverable errors return typed and fatal failures remain distinguishable.

questions.text: What is the shape and lifetime of the typed artifact reference for blob downloads, and who owns its storage?
questions.reason: Decides host storage and cleanup and whether references can appear in results or facts; the ADR only says blob downloads return metadata and binaries use a typed artifact reference.

questions.text: How does the context-free decodeMessage know whether a frame may carry a nonempty body, and where do raw body bytes live in the message types?
questions.reason: Body permission depends on method or outstanding request, which the decoder does not see; the ADR says decodeMessage validates the permitted body section but envelopes have no bytes field.

questions.text: How is cancellation delivered to a guest: protocol message, closing pipes, or signalling/killing the process with a grace period?
questions.reason: Decides whether guests need cancel handling or the host needs process-group management; the ADR requires releasing child pipes/processes and defers to ADR 0019.

questions.text: How are JSON keys and tag strings derived from Haskell field and constructor names?
questions.reason: Both peers must generate identical names; the ADR only says generated frames have unique field names.

questions.text: How does an aborting guest signal the host, and how does the host distinguish a guest abort from a crash?
questions.reason: Needed for distinguishable fatal failures; the ADR says broken frames need not be well-formed responses and stderr carries diagnostics, but defines no abort signal.
